quick: 15,000-25,000 units/kg/day IV in divided doses (max 25,000 units/kg/day)
Use only if clearly needed; safety not established
Renal function, neuro status, urine output, BUN
summary: Polymyxin B is a last-resort cyclic polypeptide antibiotic active against multidrug-resistant gram-negative bacilli including Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Dosed by body weight IV/IM with a maximum of 25,000 units/kg/day. It carries a boxed warning for nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity; parenteral use should be limited to hospitalized patients under supervision.
indications: Acute infections caused by susceptible strains of Pseudomonas aeruginosa (UTI, meningeal, bloodstream)

Serious infections caused by susceptible H. influenzae (meningeal), E. coli (urinary), Klebsiella, Enterobacter and other gram-negative organisms when less toxic drugs are ineffective or contraindicated
Ophthalmic and subconjunctival infections caused by susceptible Pseudomonas
Topical/local use in combination products for skin and eye infections

dosage.c: IV adults and children, normal renal function

dosage.d: 50,000 units once daily x3-4 days, then alternate days
dosage.n: Continue 2 weeks after CSF normal/cultures negative

dosage.d: Reduce dose below 15,000 units/kg/day per degree of impairment

admin: Reserve parenteral therapy for hospitalized patients under constant physician supervision
For IV, dissolve 500,000 units in 300-500 mL of 5% dextrose injection and infuse over ~60-90 minutes (continuous drip)
For intrathecal use, dissolve in preservative-free sodium chloride 0.9%
Avoid concurrent or sequential nephrotoxic and neurotoxic agents and neuromuscular blockers
Reconstituted solutions should be refrigerated and discarded after 72 hours
moa: Polymyxin B is a cationic cyclic polypeptide that binds to the lipid A portion of lipopolysaccharide in the outer membrane of gram-negative bacteria. This disrupts membrane integrity, increasing permeability, causing leakage of intracellular components and bactericidal cell death. It also binds and neutralizes circulating endotoxin.
preg: Safety in pregnancy has not been established; use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus. Animal reproduction studies are inadequate.
lact: Limited data on excretion in human milk; use with caution during breastfeeding and weigh benefit against potential infant risk.
renal: Nephrotoxicity is the major dose-limiting toxicity. Reduce the dose in renal impairment and in patients with nitrogen retention. Albuminuria, cellular casts and rising BUN with diminishing urine output indicate the need to discontinue therapy.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment; polymyxin B is eliminated largely by non-renal mechanisms but renal clearance still governs accumulation.

major: Other nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, amphotericin B, vancomycin, cisplatin) - additive nephrotoxicity
Neuromuscular blocking agents and curariform drugs - prolonged respiratory paralysis/apnea
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor renal function tests; may cause albuminuria and casts in urine.

common: Pain and irritation at injection site

monitoring: Renal function (serum creatinine, BUN), urine output and urinalysis frequently
Signs of superinfection or C. difficile-associated diarrhea
Therapeutic drug monitoring where available in critically ill patients
counsel: This is a hospital-administered injectable reserved for serious resistant infections
Report numbness, tingling, dizziness, blurred vision, muscle weakness or difficulty breathing immediately
Inform staff of any prior reaction to polymyxins or colistin
pk: Dosed in divided doses across 24 hours
Store dry powder at controlled room temperature; refrigerate reconstituted solution, discard after 72 h
pearls: BOXED WARNING: nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity; give parenterally only to hospitalized patients under physician supervision
BOXED WARNING: neuromuscular blockade can cause respiratory paralysis, especially with muscle relaxants/anesthetics - avoid concurrent curariform drugs
Dosed in units, not milligrams - calculate carefully by body weight
Last-line agent for MDR/XDR gram-negative infections (Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, Klebsiella)
missed: As a continuous or scheduled hospital infusion, missed doses are managed by the clinical team; resume the schedule as ordered and do not double the rate or dose without medical direction.
overdose: Overdose can cause acute renal failure, neuromuscular blockade with respiratory paralysis and apnea. Treat supportively with airway/ventilatory support; calcium salts may transiently reverse neuromuscular blockade. Discontinue the drug and maintain renal perfusion.
